title: Transmission pathways
moduleTitle: Shared: Job management and service delivery
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body: Infection hazards can be transferred through hands, contaminated tools, touch surfaces, droplets or other pathways depending on the organism and setting. Routine cleaners should not diagnose disease or assume that every stain is infectious. Identify plausible transfer routes by tracing where hands, cloths and equipment move during a job. Prioritise high-touch points and prevent transfer from toilets or waste to clean preparation areas. Follow the site infection-prevention plan and escalate unknown biological hazards or outbreak-specific requirements. Cleaning removes soil; disinfection is a separate process when required by the task and product instructions.

instruction.heading: Learning focus
instruction.body: Understand contamination pathways in cleaning work. Infection hazards can be transferred through hands, contaminated tools, touch surfaces, droplets or other pathways depending on the organism and setting. Routine cleaners should not diagnose disease or assume that every stain is infectious. Identify plausible transfer routes by tracing where hands, cloths and equipment move during a job. Prioritise high-touch points and prevent transfer from toilets or waste to clean preparation areas. Follow the site infection-prevention plan and escalate unknown biological hazards or outbreak-specific requirements. Cleaning removes soil; disinfection is a separate process when required by the task and product instructions.

instruction.heading: Worked workplace scenario
instruction.body: A worker cleans a toilet flush plate and immediately wipes a door handle with the same cloth. Trace the contamination pathway and describe the correct recovery.

instruction.heading: Guided practice
instruction.body: Map five contact points in a sample site and identify where a change of cloth, gloves or hand hygiene breaks a possible transfer chain.

instruction.heading: Quality and safety checks
instruction.body: Before signing off, confirm that the method matches the authorised site scope and current product labels, that no uncontrolled hazard remains, and that evidence is factual and privacy-safe.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

procedure: Confirm that the method matches the authorised site scope and the current product labels before starting.
Follow the site infection-prevention plan, and escalate any unknown biological hazard or outbreak-specific requirement.
Trace where hands, cloths and equipment move during the job to identify plausible transfer routes.
Map the high-touch points on the site, and clean them as a priority.
Change the cloth, gloves or hand hygiene between a toilet or waste area and a clean area, so the transfer chain is broken.
Do not wipe a clean surface, such as a door handle, with a cloth that has just touched a toilet flush plate.
Do not diagnose disease or assume that a stain is infectious; stop and escalate when a hazard is uncontrolled.
Use disinfection only where the task and the product instructions require it, because cleaning removes soil and disinfection is a separate process.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

qualityStandard: Plausible transfer routes are traced through hands, cloths and equipment during the job.
High-touch points are prioritised for cleaning.
Transfer from toilets or waste to clean preparation areas is prevented.
Unknown biological hazards and outbreak-specific requirements are escalated under the site infection-prevention plan.
summary: Infection hazards can move through hands, contaminated tools, touch surfaces and droplets, depending on the organism and the setting.
Routine cleaners do not diagnose disease or assume every stain is infectious, and they trace where hands, cloths and equipment move during a job.
High-touch points are prioritised, transfer from toilets or waste to clean areas is prevented, and unknown biological hazards are escalated.

knowledgeChecks.question: What must be checked before applying this lesson in a real workplace?
options: Only that the cleaner is wearing a clean uniform and that the cleaner has a clean bucket and a clean cloth
That the method matches the authorised site scope and current product labels, with no uncontrolled hazard remaining
That the stain is confirmed as infectious before you start and that the cleaner has been told the room is clean
That a diagnosis has been given for the room's occupants and that the cleaner has seen the file

knowledgeChecks.question: What should the worker do if an uncontrolled hazard or unauthorised task is encountered?
options: Clean it up quietly to keep the job moving and finish before the next room
Finish the job first and report it at the end and clean the spot before leaving
Stop, do not proceed, and escalate under the site infection-prevention plan
Decide yourself whether it is infectious, then continue and clean it if it looks wet

knowledgeChecks.question: Which of these does the lesson name as a way infection hazards can be transferred?
